s: to man (to supply with staff or crew)
bemannen.et: From Middle High German bemannen. Equivalent to be- + Mann + -en or be- + mannen.

s: Hast du das Schild bemerkt, an dem wir gerade vorbeikamen?

to remark, to mention, to note

bemerken.et: From Middle High German bemerken, from Old High German bimerken, from Proto-West Germanic *bimarkijan. Equivalent to be- + merken. Cognate with Dutch bemerken, also related to Middle Dutch and Middle High German bemarken, and English bemark.

bemitleidenswert.et: bemitleiden (“to feel compassion”) + -wert (“-worthy”), ultimately derived from Mitleid (“compassion”).

to employ, to cite, to trot out (of arguments, approaches, examples, now especially of ones considered trite or unconvincing)
to betake oneself (to a location despite inconvenience)
to call for, to ask for (someone's presence or aid)
bemühen.et: From be- + Mühe + -en. Compare Dutch bemoeien.

s: Eine Kultur der Gewalt bemächtigt sich des Landes.

to assess, to measure, to proportion
to measure on the base of something
bemessen.et: From Middle High German *bemëȥȥen, from Old High German bimëȥȥan, from Proto-West Germanic *bimetan. Equivalent to be- + messen. Cognate with Dutch bemeten and obsolete English bemete.

s: a topped bread, synonym of Butterbrot
Bemme.et: A West Slavic borrowing, synonymous to Upper Sorbian pomazka, Lower Sorbian pomazka, Masovian Polish pomazanka.
